title: Soil erosion control at landscape scale
bottleneck: Soil erosion is the most severe and interconnected threat to soil health — 81% of FAO regional assessments judge erosion management poor or very poor, with a deteriorating trend since 2015 — yet control requires coordinated action across whole landscapes and watersheds, not individual farms. Terraces, cover crops, and no-till work locally but adoption is low, and erosion's worst damage is diffuse and delayed, so nobody pays for prevention.
why_it_blocks: Topsoil forms over centuries and is lost in seasons. Unchecked erosion permanently destroys the productive base that yields depend on.
current_state: Proven practices like reduced tillage, cover crops, and agroforestry exist, but FAO finds low adoption in over half of assessments while erosion worsens. Terraces, cover crops, and no-till work locally, but landscape-scale coordination remains the missing piece.
